title: Connection fairness and stream-shed demo
summary: Short demo focused on connection fairness, stream shedding/backpressure, and long-context behavior at high TPS. Agreed to run a 48-hour benchmark with realistic sessions, validate KV caching improvements and an autoscale policy. Customer leaning towards Dedicated pilot if latency and tail-percentiles meet SLAs.
action_items: Maya - share pilot pricing and Dedicated capacity options by 2027-12-02
Jonas - provide synthetic load config and traffic generator script by 2027-12-05
Priya - send sample anonymized session traces and typical prompt lengths by 2027-12-01
next_steps: Schedule 2-hour kickoff for benchmark (AE+SE+SRE+customer) week of 2027-12-04
Run 48h pilot with 5k TPS synthetic load + 200 long sessions concurrently
Share Console dashboard template and Optimize recommendations doc
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-11-28 10:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonas Rey (Redwood SE), Arman Singh (Redwood Product), Priya Rao (Astrid Labs Eng), Carlos Mendes (Astrid Labs CTO), Ellen Park (Astrid SRE), Samir (PM)

[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call, uh, we'll run through an interactive demo showing connection fairness and how our runtime sheds streaming when there's backpressure, we'll peep the Console and run a couple of synthetic bursts.
[00:12] Priya: thanks, Maya, excited — we've been hitting regular tail latency spikes when long chat sessions overlap with our high TPS inference path.
[00:23] Jonas (SE): cool, yeah so our focus is: how do we avoid long-history sessions starving the short interaction flows, and how graceful is the shedding? We'll show KV cache behavior, batching, and autoscale triggers.
[00:37] Carlos: quick context from us — we have a mix of short assistant requests (200-500ms target) and long transcript summarization sessions that keep state for 80k tokens occasionally, average session length 12k tokens. Peak TPS target for pilot is around 5k.
[00:54] Ellen: and SRE note — we need predictable p95/p99 for the short path, otherwise user experience drops, and our ops team needs clear telemetry.
[01:08] Jonas: got it. I'll start with the Console to show current metrics and then flip to a live run. Bear with me while I pull up the dashboard.
[01:30] [Console screen share noises; some cross-talk]
[01:45] Jonas: this is the per-route view, you can see hotspots, here's a route we pinned for short assistant requests, here's the long-context route, see the token distribution histogram — you can be surprised, some names in the trace are wrong — uh, 'K V cash' pops up in auto transcripts but that's KV cache.
[02:10] Priya: heh, yep we saw that in your docs too. Question: what happens when the long-history sessions accumulate and the KV store grows? Do you evict aggressively or keep high hit rate?
[02:26] Jonas: our default is workload-aware eviction: least-recently-used-ish and we also have a small TTL on prefix entries; but the trick is when a node is saturated we degrade long-history fetches first. That keeps short requests moving. It's basically connection fairness plus priority shedding.
[02:45] Maya: to add, Optimize can recommend quantization and batching tweaks per-model that reduce per-token cost and lower CPU/GPU footprint which indirectly reduces the need to shed.
[03:00] Samir: at what point does shedding become visible as errors to the user vs graceful truncation?
[03:12] Jonas: two modes — we either fall back to a shorter model variant (if configured) or we return a partial result with a structured flag like "truncated_due_to_backpressure":true so the app can retry or degrade gracefully. For streaming we can emit a final event informing the client to re-open a short-session call.
[03:36] Ellen: do you have an SDK hook for that? A client-side backoff advice?
[03:42] Jonas: yes, SDKs include a reconnect token and guidelines, and the Console shows per-token shed counts. We'll demo the streaming traces.
[04:00] [Demo: synthetic load starting]
[04:15] Jonas: starting phase one: baseline 500 TPS with 1% long sessions. Watch p95 on the short route.
[04:45] [15s silence while generator warms up; server log noise in background]
[05:05] Maya: little note: the transcript may mislabel some micro metrics — like 'epochal context' in the ASR — ignore that, it's just firefly transcription idiosyncrasy.
[05:20] Priya: p95 is at 380ms now, good.
[05:28] Jonas: now ramping to 3k TPS and injecting 80 concurrent long-history sessions (10k-40k tokens each).
[05:50] [ambient typing]
[06:05] Priya: ok I see slightly rising tail, p99 creeping up to ~1.3s for short route.
[06:14] Jonas: yep, this is where KV cache hit rate matters — when long sessions hit the cache massively it's fine; if they all miss, you'll see memory and KV fetch latency spike.
[06:30] Maya: Arman, want to show the Optimize recommendations for this workload?
[06:37] Arman (Product): sure, we suggested an aggressive prefix caching policy for your long sessions, plus a mixed-quant profile: int8 for the short model path and a lightly quantized fp16-ish variant for the long-history model. That reduces tail by about 20% in our internal runs.
[06:55] Priya: do you have numbers? like p99 delta?
[06:59] Arman: in similar configs we saw p99 drop from ~1.4s to ~950ms on the short route under load, and long-path median improved as well because fewer disk hits.
[07:20] Carlos: those look promising. When you say 'mixed-quant profile' is that automatic or we apply it via the Console?
[07:28] Arman: you can apply via the Console Optimize recommendations page; we automaton suggestion but customer must approve rollout. There's also canary rollout support.
[07:40] [09:00] Jonas: ramping to 5k TPS now and enabling synthetic network jitter to simulate inter-region variance.
[09:15] [system beeps and occasional overlaps]
[09:28] Ellen: we're seeing short route p99 spike to 2.1s, that's more than we'd accept.
[09:35] Jonas: yep, that's the stress point. Now I'm flipping on connection-fairness policy which caps per-connection token emission and prioritizes short sessions.
[09:50] [pause]
[10:05] Priya: immediate drop in p99 to 760ms, nice. Is there any client-visible signal?
[10:12] Jonas: yes, you'll see an event in the streaming frames: "shed_reason:connection_fairness" and a header with suggested retry-after in ms. Also Console shows per-session preemption.
[10:30] Samir: for audits we need logs that include which sessions were shed and why — is that available?
[10:38] Maya: yes, audit logs include session id, route, shed_reason, node id and approximate latency. We can redact user-payloads for privacy.
[10:48] Carlos: how does this interact with Dedicated nodes? If we move to Dedicated GPU pool, does fairness still apply cluster-wide?
[10:58] Jonas: fairness is policy-driven — on Dedicated you can set stricter isolation per-tenant; we'll still apply fairness within the node to avoid one session consuming all sockets.
[11:12] Priya: any limits on concurrent async KV fetches per node? We saw disk saturation in our setup before.
[11:20] Jonas: we limit concurrent KV fetches and queue them; when queue depth passes threshold we shift to degraded mode where long-history fetches are served from a locally-generated skeleton instead of full reconstruction. So the tail doesn't rip the whole system.
[11:40] Ellen: that sounds like a pattern we want — degrade instead of fail. Will that affect semantic quality?
[11:47] Jonas: yes slightly, but it's prioritized to keep short interactive flows intact. Your UX team can detect the degraded flag and ask for a background reprocess.
[11:58] Priya: what's the recommended autoscale policy for this sort of mixed workload?
[12:04] Arman: we recommend CPU+GPU-aware scale triggers: token_queue_depth and p95_latency over a 60s window. For your profile, a two-stage policy works best: maintain a base Dedicated pool for short paths and let burst autoscale add ephemeral nodes for long-batch sessions.
[12:26] Samir: cost wise how does ephemerals compare versus Dedicated headroom?
[12:32] Maya: depends on usage; ephemerals are cheaper for short bursty spikes because you pay for actual runtime, but Dedicated reduces per-token unit cost at steady state. We'll provide modeled numbers in the pricing sheet.
[12:48] [Demo: enable aggressive long-session eviction]
[13:05] Jonas: watch the stream — I'm forcing eviction of old prefixes to simulate hot churn.
[13:20] Priya: oh we see a bump in long-path misses, but short route stays stable thanks to eviction priority.
[13:32] Ellen: what's the effect on KV hit rate over time?
[13:36] Jonas: hit rate drops from 82% to ~51% after eviction but short-route p95 stays within bounds because we prioritized their entries.
[13:48] Carlos: can we set session-weighted priorities? e.g., premium customers get protected cache entries?
[13:55] Jonas: yep, RBAC+priority classes are supported — Console lets you tag routes and set protection policies.
[14:08] Maya: quick micro note, folks: the transcript may show random speakers as Speaker 1 — ignore the mislabels.
[14:14] [ambient questions from customer about logs and retention]
[14:30] Priya: retention policies — we want 90 days of traces but only 30 days of content. How granular is that?
[14:40] Maya: you can set per-route retention: traces, token-level telemetry, and raw payloads. For PII compliance you can route raw payloads to your KMS-protected store or to a customer-managed on-prem archive.
[14:58] Samir: earlier you mentioned fallback to shorter model variant — how do you ensure semantic consistency? We don't want hallucination regressions.
[15:08] Arman: Optimize runs a similarity eval between model variants and flags major deltas. We also support staged canaries with traffic rings and automated quality checks against your prompt set.
[15:28] Carlos: good. Could we run a split where 5% of traffic is short-variant canary with Eval sets?
[15:34] Jonas: yes, Console supports traffic split and automatic rollback on metric regressions.
[15:42] [Live failure injection: network jitter + node OOM]
[15:55] Jonas: throwing a node OOM to test fallback, you might see a temporary routing to the fallback region.
[16:10] Priya: saw a spike, and then calls rerouted, some retries returned 502 for a few seconds — what was that?
[16:18] Jonas: transient 502s happen during route recalculation; we have automatic retry policies but for low-latency flows we recommend client-side exponential backoff with jitter.
[16:32] Ellen: will that count as an error in our SLAs?
[16:36] Maya: if within configured retry/fallback window it's not counted as steady-state error; we can exclude short reconvergence windows in enterprise SLA definitions.
[16:50] Samir: what metrics should we instrument on our side?
[16:54] Jonas: session open/close, shed events count, per-request latency, token counts, and error/retry samples. We'll share a telemetry schema.
[17:10] Priya: we'll send sample traces after the call.
[17:14] [Question from Carlos about encrypted KV stores]
[17:20] Jonas: KV can be backed by customer-managed KMS and HSMs on Private; for Hosted we support envelope encryption with managed KMS, and on Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS.
[17:34] Maya: security docs will be included in the packet.
[17:38] Priya: demo notes — could you show the Console view for the shed counts?
[17:44] Jonas: switching, here is the per-node shed rate by reason; connection_fairness spikes during the 5k TPS run and then declines when we enabled per-connection caps.
[18:05] Priya: we want the raw CSV of shed events for ingestion into our SIEM.
[18:10] Maya: noted, we'll share that.
[18:18] [Quick break in transcript; background chatter]
[18:40] Jonas: one more thing — streaming timeouts: we expose idle and total timeouts client-side. You can tune them per-route. For long-history sessions increase idle timeout and use a keepalive ping to avoid premature stream closure.
[19:00] Ellen: what's default idle timeout?
[19:04] Jonas: default is 60s, but we recommend 5m for long-history notebooks. If you set it too high it increases resource hold time so there's a cost trade-off.
[19:20] Samir: can we run with 3m for the pilot?
[19:24] Maya: yes, we'll recommend 3m for your pilot.
[19:30] [Load test tail analysis begins]
[20:05] Jonas: ingesting Astrid sample traces now to replay realistic tokens.
[20:18] Priya: heads-up some traces are scrubbed; you'll see placeholders.
[20:24] Jonas: replay underway — note the p99 on the short route is stable at 860ms with the configured policies.
[20:40] Carlos: that's a lot better than earlier. Can you share the exact config?
[20:46] Jonas: yes, it's in the load config: short_route_priority=true, per_connection_cap=128_tokens_per_sec, kv_prefix_ttl=300s, eviction_policy=weighted_lru. I'll attach the script.
[21:05] Priya: any special flags for streaming clients when reconnecting?
[21:10] Jonas: include last_event_id and reconnection_token; the server will resume from the KV snapshot if available. If snapshot isn't available, you'll get truncated flag.
[21:26] Ellen: does resumed session bill as new tokens?
[21:30] Maya: billing counts emitted tokens; resumed tokens that are re-sent are billed. We can do a discount on pilot for duplicate replays if that helps.
[21:46] Carlos: acceptable.
[21:50] [Around minute 22, customer asks about legal/procurement timeline]
[22:05] Samir: what's typical procurement time for Dedicated?
[22:10] Maya: on average 6-8 weeks for enterprise procurement and setup, faster if you use our standard contract. Pilot can start in 2-3 weeks.
[22:22] Priya: we want pilot first to measure tail and cost.
[22:25] Maya: agreed. We'll send pilot pricing.
[22:30] [Demo wrap-up: propose pilot parameters]
[22:40] Jonas: proposed pilot: 48h continuous run, synthetic 5k TPS + 200 concurrent long sessions (avg 12k tokens), Dedicated baseline of 4 GPUs with 2 ephemeral nodes for bursts, KV backed by customer-managed KMS.
[22:58] Priya: we like that. Please include a run where KV cache is disabled so we can compare.
[23:05] Maya: we'll do A/B with cache on/off; Jonas will provide env and scripts.
[23:15] Carlos: and include the shed CSV events and console dashboards.
[23:20] Maya: noted.
[23:25] Samir: any remaining security blockers?
[23:28] Priya: SOC2 and ISO files we need to review.
[23:32] Maya: we'll attach SOC2/ISO certs and the Private deployment checklist.
[23:36] [Final recap]
[23:40] Maya: recap: Maya to share pilot pricing and contract options; Jonas to share load scripts, Console dashboard template, and shed CSV; Priya to send traces and sample prompts; schedule 2-hour kickoff week of 2027-12-04.
[23:55] Carlos: thanks all, this was helpful.
[24:02] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up.

End of recording.
